question: How Does a MEMS Gyroscope Work?
body_html:
A MEMS gyroscope measures angular rate by detecting the Coriolis force on a silicon proof mass vibrating at its resonant frequency, typically 10 to 40 kHz.

When the chip rotates, the force deflects the mass perpendicular to the drive motion, and capacitive electrodes sense this deflection: F = 2 × m × v × ω.

Example: m = 1 µg, v = 1 mm/s and ω = 1.745 rad/s (100 deg/s) give F = 2 × 10⁻⁹ × 0.001 × 1.745 = 3.49 × 10⁻¹² N.
